name: Pico do Fogo and Chã das Caldeiras
subtitle: Pico do Fogo is a 2,829-metre volcano on the island of Fogo.

facts.label: What
facts.value: Chã das Caldeiras ('Chã') is a community inside the crater of Pico do Fogo, a 2,829 m volcano on the island of Fogo

facts.label: Setting
facts.value: Chã is a flat area between the Pico and the Bordeira cliffs, formed by lavas ponding there

facts.label: Settlement
facts.value: Settled for about 150 years; eruptions from vents near the base of Pico occurred in 1951, 1995 and 2014-2015

facts.label: Population 1995
facts.value: About 1,300 people lived in Chã at the time of the 1995 eruption, in three villages

facts.label: 1995 relocation
facts.value: After 1995, services such as health and education were permanently moved out of Chã to planned villages on the arid south side of Fogo

facts.label: Agriculture
facts.value: Chã is one of the most productive agricultural areas in semi-arid Cape Verde

facts.label: Livelihoods
facts.value: Residents relied on tourism, remittances, vegetable and fruit exports and the agricultural co-operative, whose wine was the most important product by value

facts.label: National park HQ
facts.value: New Fogo National Park headquarters inaugurated in March 2014; lava submerged it a week into the eruption

facts.label: 2014-2015 damage
facts.value: Lava engulfed 75% (260) of buildings in three villages, 25% of cultivable land, water storage and the only road into the area

facts.label: Return
facts.value: Residents were reluctant to be resettled on the arid south side of Fogo after recent eruptions

parts.text: Pico do Fogo is a 2,829-metre volcano on the island of Fogo. Inside its crater lies Chã das Caldeiras, a farming community known as Chã, built on a plain between the peak and the Bordeira cliffs. Lava from the 2014-2015 eruption engulfed 75% of the buildings in three villages there.
